data.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 3 at 2:20AM EST until November 3 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Minor to Moderate coastal flooding, large breaking waves
of up to 6 feet in the surf zone, and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
data.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 031221
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
721 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 720 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

  - Potential for additional heavy rainfall and flooding continue
    today with rounds of showers and thunderstorms, mainly late
    this morning through the evening hours.

  - Minor to Moderate coastal flooding expected during times of 
    high tide.

  - Dangerous marine and beach conditions are expected across the
    Atlantic coast today.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 401 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

Model consensus remains consistent in showing a mid-lvl disturbance 
moving across the area to begin gradually dissipating through mid 
week. This is mainly driven by an interaction of the disturbance 
with an approaching northern stream frontal boundary. But model 
soundings still keep abundant moisture in place, with PWATs 
well above normals, still lingering around 2" today and Wednesday. 

Ensembles amd high-res solutions depict a feature resembling a 
cutoff low aloft over the E Gulf providing enough dynamic lifting 
across the state today. Meanwhile, forecast CAPE around 1500 J/Kg, 
along with having better chances at periods of more efficient 
daytime heating during the morning hours. Therefore, expect 
another round of heavy downpours this afternoon and evening with 
widespread Max POPs in the 60-70% range. Particularly vulnerable 
to localized flooding impacts will again be east coast metro 
areas, which were significantly impacted yesterday. 

In terms of severe weather potential, sounding and model data show 
some lingering low-lvl CIN, along with a narrow layer of mid-lvl 
drier air, which may provide some capping to vertical updrafts. This 
may help in preventing explosive development, however, it may favor 
localized, highly efficient convective downpours. Flooding threat 
will be particularly high with consecutive showers and slow-
moving storms, with isolated max accumulations around 5" possible.

Also, coastal hazards continue as high astronomical tides combine 
with persistent onshore winds to keep threat of coastal flooding in 
place today. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday night through Monday)
Issued at 401 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

Long range models depict a synoptic scenario with a series of 
shortwave troughs aloft passing through the area late this week and 
into the weekend, while some drier air filters into the mid/low 
lvls. Meanwhile, model consensus is increasing regarding the 
potential for a dry frontal passage for the later part of the work 
week. 

There is also a potential shortwave cutting off from the northern 
stream and slowly moving across the E CONUS, which will ultimately 
decide when/if we get the FROPA all the way into SoFlo later this
week. Regardless of the final outcome, models still keep this 
FROPA fairly dry with little indications of significant 
rain/thunderstorm activity associated with it. Winds are also 
expected to diminish as pressure gradients relax in the wake of 
the frontal passage. 

Temperatures will generally remain in the mid to upper 80s,
warmest over southern areas of SoFlo. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 720 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

Gusty east-northeasterly winds of 10-15 kts are expected to prevail 
after 15Z at all terminals. SHRA/TSRA may produce periods of 
MVFR/IFR cigs/vis and erratic winds through this afternoon into 
the evening. Winds are expected to diminish overnight to around 10
kts out of the east.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 327 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Hazardous marine conditions will continue across the Atlantic waters 
through this evening as a fresh to strong easterly breeze and a NE
swell remain in place. Across the Gulf waters, a moderate to 
fresh easterly breeze will gradually diminish today. Scattered to
numerous showers and thunderstorms will continue across all local
waters through the early portion of the week. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 327 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

The onshore flow and elevated winds and seas will keep a High Risk
for rip currents across Atlantic beaches through at least mid
week. Higher than usual tides will also create elevated water 
levels near the coast. Dangerous beach and swim conditions are 
expected through mid-week.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Issued at 327 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Water levels are forecast to gradually climb into Moderate flood 
stage again by tonight's high tide as we start to head closer and 
closer to the New Moon on Nov 9. Hopefully, by mid-week, we'll be
able to remove the strong onshore wind component and pull back 
some of the heavy rain potential as astronomical tide levels start
to rise again.

&&

ABNT20 KNHC 031712
TWOAT 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
100 PM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Western Atlantic:
An area of low pressure is expected to form along a weakening 
frontal boundary a few hundred miles south of Bermuda over the next 
day or so. This system could gradually acquire some subtropical 
characteristics late this week or this weekend while it moves slowly 
eastward over the western to central Subtropical Atlantic. By early 
next week, environmental conditions are forecast to become 
unfavorable for further development. For more information on this 
system, including Gale Warnings, please see High Seas Forecast 
issued by the National Weather Service. 
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
Forecaster Papin
